item.title: Stop Letting Models Grade Their Own Homework: Why LLM-as-a-Judge Fails at Prompt Injection Defense
item.description:
Author: Lakera Team
Date: January 16, 2026
Tags: ["AI Security", "Prompt Injection", "Large Language Models", "Adversarial Attacks", "AI Safety"]
Summary:
  • Many security teams use LLMs to screen for prompt injection attacks.
  • This approach seems logical at first.
  • However, it fails under adversarial conditions.
  • Using LLMs to judge other LLMs creates fragile defenses.
  • These defenses often fail silently, risking false security.
  • Alternative methods are needed for robust protection.

item.title: Understanding Lumo AI Assistant: Announcing pyLumo
item.description:
Author: Rich Smith
Date: N/A
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Privacy and Security", "Software Development", "Open Source", "Cryptography"]
Summary:
  • Mindgard explored Lumo AI assistant by Proton, focusing on privacy features.
  • Lumo uses a unique user-to-LLM encryption scheme.
  • No official APIs existed, so Mindgard created pyLumo library.
  • pyLumo enables programmatic interaction with Lumo in Python.
  • pyLumoTUI offers a terminal UI for chatting with Lumo.
  • Proton’s encryption ensures message privacy from intermediaries.

item.title: What is Excessive Agency? AI agents are gaining autonomy, but without proper controls that autonomy becomes a security risk. This article explores what excessive agency is, how it emerges in real systems, and why it is one of the most critical challenges in agentic AI today.
item.description:
Author: Alessandro Pignati
Date: January 16, 2026
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "AI Safety", "Autonomous Systems", "Risk Management", "Agentic AI"]
Summary:
  • AI agents are gaining increasing autonomy in decision-making.
  • Excessive agency occurs when control over agents is insufficient.
  • This leads to risks from unchecked, persistent, or opaque actions.
  • Such agents can operate without user confirmation and accumulate context.
  • Excessive agency is a systemic design and governance issue.
  • It differs from bugs or prompt errors and involves authority without accountability.
